title: Tokengrid attribution compact pane — prototype and export patterns
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype a compact token-level attribution pane (Tokengrid) for Redwood Console that surfaces per-route / per-model / per-environment micro-spend, supports role-aware filters, and provides CSV/Parquet export patterns suitable for downstream chargeback. The goal is a dense, scannable UI that fits inside the Console right rail and the expanded Cost Drill view. The pane should: show top contributors by token spend, mini-sparklines for time series, an attribution waterfall for prompt vs completion tokens, per-message sample drilldown, and one-click export templates (billing CSV, customer-ready report). Prototype must include responsive states, hover detail cards, and a loading/fallback strategy when real-time microcounts are expensive to compute.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Tokengrid prototype (Figma) with compact and expanded states; 2) Hover detail card with exact token counts and cost breakdown for selected row; 3) Role-aware presets (owner, finance, eng) wired as filter examples in the prototype; 4) Export spec (CSV/Parquet column schema) documented and linked; 5) Performance notes describing server-aggregation fallback and UX placeholders for streaming flows; 6) Review feedback addressed by PM and Eng and sign-off recorded.
engineering_notes: Prefer server-side aggregation snapshots (minute granularity) to avoid per-request token rehydration. Suggested API endpoints: /v1/console/costs/tokengrid/summary and /v1/console/costs/tokengrid/rows?time_range=.. . Work with infra to add a caching layer keyed by route+model+interval. Fallback: show estimated counts from sampling when exact counts delayed.
decisions: 1) Use compact grid (dense rows with optional expanded row) rather than a full table to maximize information density in the right rail. 2) Compute conservative per-token cost server-side with an audit column that links back to raw ledger IDs. 3) Expose two export presets: 'finance-ready' (aggregated, grouped by customer and route) and 'audit-trace' (row-level with ledger IDs and message payload hashes).
review_comments: PM (Harpreet Singh): prefer clearer language for finance export column names; asked for a sample CSV mock. Eng (Sofia Alvarez): flagged latency risk when users query wide time ranges—requested pagination and snapshot TTL. Security (Anika Patel): requested KMS-hash field in audit-trace export and SSO RBAC checks for export action.
next_steps: 1) Iterate Figma mock to include finance CSV sample and update column names (action: Maya). 2) Add placeholder UI for 'estimated' vs 'exact' tokens and work with infra to define snapshot TTL (action: Liam). 3) Create a small product PRD section describing export retention and compliance considerations (action: Harpreet). 4) Schedule design review with Finance and Compliance next week.
notes: Prototype includes accessibility contrast checks, keyboard navigation for row focus, and a minimal mobile collapse behavior. Consider adding a 'cost-snapshot' toggle to freeze values for export to ensure reproducible billing reports.
change_log: 2025-02-10: Created ticket and initial hypothesis (Maya). 2025-02-18: First Figma pass complete; posted for feedback. 2025-02-24: Eng raised latency concerns; added server-aggregation note. 2025-03-02: Added export presets and sample CSV; security requested additional audit fields. 2025-03-04: Updated prototype per comments; submitted for formal design review.
implementation_risks: High-cardinality routes can cause large result sets—mitigation: enforce server-side pagination, snapshot aggregation, and UI limit with 'show more'. Exporting very large intervals should trigger an async job with email/download link rather than blocking UI.
qa_checklist: 1) Verify hover card shows exact token counts when snapshot available. 2) Confirm export CSV matches schema in Confluence. 3) Validate that RBAC blocks export action for non-authorized roles. 4) Ensure keyboard-only navigation highlights rows and opens expanded view. 5) Confirm fallback state displays 'estimated' badge when sampling used.
notes_for_engineering: Start with a backend feature flag for tokengrid-summary to allow canary rollout. Use sampling as a short-term measure; long-term prefer minute-aggregates with an internal ETL that emits per-route per-model counts to the cost ledger. Provide a lightweight GraphQL/REST shape for UI to request only top N rows with totals.
ux_choreography: Row interactions: hover -> detail card; click row -> expand inline with per-message examples; right-arrow -> open full drill view. Export button flows into modal with presets and retention checkbox. Use subtle motion for expanding rows (150ms) and skeleton loaders for streaming data.
